headline: New Year's Day under sail
summary: The Ibis sails on, about seven miles past Roda.

headline: Stuck again, jackals at night
summary: The boat grounds on a sandbar and the crew must haul and pole it free. Roosevelt hears jackals.

events.detail: Boat hauled and poled off a sandbank

headline: Bumps and groundings on the Nile
summary: The day's excitement comes from collisions, groundings and similar mishaps on the river.

events.detail: Collisions and groundings on the river

headline: Becalmed below the cliffs of Abu Feda
summary: With no wind opposite Abu Feda, the crew tows and poles the boat. The day closes with a splendid sunset over the cliffs.

events.detail: No wind; boat towed and poled
Watches a sunset over the cliffs

headline: A broken tiller at Asyut
summary: At Asyut the Ibis breaks its tiller, and Roosevelt sees a mirage.

headline: Donkeys to the tombs of Asyut
summary: Above Asyut, Roosevelt rides a donkey out to ancient tombs covered in hieroglyphs, and he scorns the scrawls left by modern visitors.

events.detail: Rides a donkey to the tombs
Examines hieroglyphs and notes modern graffiti

headline: Sailing past Girga
summary: The Ibis sails on below Girga.

headline: Good wind and a sketch of the ibis
summary: With a good breeze above Girga, Roosevelt goes shooting and writes a description of the ibis.
uncertain: 'Describes Ibis' could mean the bird or the boat.

headline: Fair wind above Qena
summary: The boat makes good time with a strong wind above Qena.

headline: Karnak by moonlight
summary: At Thebes Roosevelt walks ashore past the temple of Medinet Habu and the two seated colossi, hands resting on their knees. The boat ties up beside the Temple of Luxor, and that night he sees Karnak under the moon.

events.detail: Walks past Medinet Habu and the seated colossi
Moors by the Temple of Luxor

headline: Across the river to the Valley of the Kings
summary: Roosevelt crosses the Nile, sees temples on the Valley of the Kings side, and collects several birds.

events.detail: Crosses the Nile to the west bank

headline: A Sunday stroll in Luxor
summary: Roosevelt spends the day walking around Luxor.

headline: Royal tombs and a wolf
summary: Roosevelt visits the tomb of Ramesses III and Belzoni's tomb, and on the way back shoots a wolf.

events.detail: Visits the tombs of Ramesses III and Belzoni's tomb

uncertain: 'Belzoni's tomb' is the tomb of Seti I, found by Giovanni Belzoni.

headline: Towed to Armant
summary: The boat is tracked upstream to Armant, where Theodore Sr. shoots a hawk.

headline: A long walk at Sharuna
summary: At Sharuna Roosevelt makes a long hike across a sandbank.

headline: Doves and a misfire near Edfu
summary: Above Edfu Roosevelt walks along the shore and gets some doves, though his gun misfires once.

events.detail: Shoots doves on a shore walk

headline: A full day's sail to Aswan
summary: The Ibis sails from morning to evening to reach Aswan.

events.detail: Reaches Aswan after sailing all day

headline: Philae by moonlight on Bamie's birthday
summary: Roosevelt hunts in the desert outside Aswan. Everyone dines aboard the Ibis, and by moonlight he sees the ruins at Philae. It is Bamie's eighteenth birthday.

events.detail: Dinner for all aboard the Ibis
Sees the Philae ruins by moonlight

uncertain: Misdated in the source: Bamie's 18th birthday falls on January 18, 1873; that part of this entry belongs to that date.

headline: Elephantine Island and Philae by day
summary: After sleeping through much of the morning, Roosevelt visits Elephantine Island and returns to Philae to see it in daylight.

headline: A jackal in the desert
summary: Hunting in the desert near Aswan, Roosevelt sees a jackal.

headline: At the cataracts
summary: Roosevelt visits the Nile cataracts at Aswan.

headline: Desert hunting at Aswan
summary: Roosevelt spends the day hunting in the desert.

headline: Turning back downriver
summary: After one more desert hunt, the Ibis heads downstream in the afternoon. The family has to turn around because Theodore Sr. must be in Vienna by May 1.

headline: Kom Ombo at sunset
summary: Roosevelt hunts along the river and sees the ruins of Kom Ombo at sunset; the boat sails through the night.

events.detail: Sees Kom Ombo's ruins at sunset

headline: A cheerful letter to Aunt Annie
summary: Near Kom Ombo Roosevelt visits a ruin and writes to Aunt Annie Gracie that he is having a fine time.

letters.topic: Reports how much he is enjoying the Nile journey

uncertain: Name of the ruin ('Hagen Lillibis') is garbled.

headline: Edfu's temple, then shooting
summary: Roosevelt tours the temple at Edfu in the morning and shoots in the afternoon.

headline: El Kab's tombs and on to Isna
summary: Roosevelt sees the temple and tombs of El Kab, and the boat reaches Isna in the afternoon.

events.detail: Visits the temple and tombs at El Kab

headline: The temple of Khnum
summary: At Isna Roosevelt sees the temple of Khnum and goes shooting.

headline: Back at Thebes
summary: Returning to Thebes, Roosevelt spends the day shooting.

headline: Fifteen birds and outgrown clothes
summary: On a daylong shooting trip at Thebes Roosevelt takes fifteen birds and visits Medinet Habu. He has shot up so much on the journey that his clothes no longer fit.

events.detail: Kills fifteen birds on an all-day outing
Has outgrown his clothes during the trip

headline: Karnak and specimens
summary: At Thebes Roosevelt tours Karnak and collects some specimens. His sister Corinne writes to Edith Carow back home.

headline: Sunday services and Karnak again
summary: The family holds Sunday services, and Roosevelt returns to Karnak.

headline: A crane, snipe and pigeons
summary: Roosevelt goes out shooting and brings back a crane, snipe and pigeons, while his father and Ellie visit a tomb on the far bank.

events.detail: Shoots a crane, snipe and pigeons
Theodore Sr. and Ellie visit a tomb across the Nile

headline: The temple of Dendera
summary: Stopping two days at Qena, the family visits the Temple of Dendera, and Roosevelt goes shooting.

headline: Shooting at Qena
summary: Roosevelt spends the day shooting at Qena.

headline: Rowing down to El Balyana
summary: The boat is rowed downstream to El Balyana, and Roosevelt shoots.

headline: Abydos and sixteen pigeons
summary: Roosevelt sees the temple at Abydos and kills sixteen pigeons.

headline: Meeting the Zingara
summary: After a morning of shooting, the crew rows all day, and the Ibis falls in with the boat Zingara.

headline: Father preaches to the Rachel's party
summary: The passengers of the Rachel come aboard to hear Theodore Sr. read a sermon. Roosevelt writes to Aunt Annie Gracie.

events.detail: Theodore Sr. reads a sermon to visitors from the Rachel

headline: Shooting and tea
summary: Roosevelt goes shooting and later takes tea.

headline: Shooting at Beni Hasan
summary: At Beni Hasan Roosevelt heads out to shoot.

headline: Rowing Ralph Waldo Emerson to lunch
summary: After touring the Beni Hasan tombs and shooting an owl, Roosevelt helps host Ralph Waldo Emerson and his daughter Ellen for lunch, rowing them over to the family boat himself. Ellen later wrote home describing the ruddy-cheeked, blue-eyed boy at the oars.

events.detail: Visits the tombs of Beni Hasan
The Roosevelts invite Ralph Waldo Emerson and his daughter Ellen to lunch
Rows the Emersons over in the children's small boat

uncertain: Ellen Emerson's letter calls the family boat 'Abou Erdan'; elsewhere it is the Ibis.

headline: Collision with the Moorkat
summary: Roosevelt shoots with his father near Beni Suef. The Ibis runs into another boat, the Moorkat, which smashes the front cabin.

events.detail: The Ibis collides with the Moorkat, damaging its front cabin

headline: Rough sailing toward Memphis
summary: The boat sails all day toward Memphis, with choppy water in the afternoon.

events.detail: Sails all day; rough in the afternoon

headline: The Serapeum and back to Cairo
summary: At Memphis Roosevelt sees the Serapeum and the Apis pits, kills two ibises and arrives back in Cairo in the afternoon.

events.detail: Sees the Serapeum and Apis burial pits

uncertain: OCR 'Serapiu and Apir Pits' read as the Serapeum and Apis pits.

headline: Church in Cairo, still aboard
summary: The family goes to church in Cairo and continues living on the boat.

headline: Rainy day of collecting
summary: Still on the dahabeah, Roosevelt kills birds on a rainy day.

headline: Back to Shepheard's Hotel
summary: The family leaves the boat for Shepheard's Hotel; it rains.

events.detail: Moves from the dahabeah to Shepheard's Hotel

headline: Lounging around a wet Cairo
summary: Roosevelt idles about the city in the rain.

headline: Calling on Dr. Grant
summary: On another rainy day Roosevelt visits Dr. Grant's.

headline: First look at the Suez Canal
summary: At Ismailia, Roosevelt sees the Suez Canal and stays at the Hotel Pagnon. The women of the family go by way of Alexandria to Port Said, where the men will meet them.

events.detail: Goes to Ismailia and stays at the Hotel Pagnon
The ladies travel via Alexandria to Port Said

headline: Up the canal to Port Said
summary: Roosevelt takes a steamer up the canal to Port Said and stays at the Hotel de France. His asthma flares.

events.detail: Steamer along the Suez Canal to Port Said

headline: Reunited aboard the steamer
summary: On board the steamer Alphe, Roosevelt and the men rejoin the rest of the party.

events.detail: Joins the family aboard the steamer Alphe

headline: Landing at Jaffa, a night in a monastery
summary: The party lands at Jaffa and rides three hours to Ramleh, lodging in a monastery. Theodore Sr. persuades the monks to let the women stay as well.

events.detail: Three-hour ride on horseback to Ramleh
Stays at a monastery after Theodore Sr. wins permission for the women

uncertain: Source adds a bracket '[Haifa, Israel]', which is wrong; Jaffa kept.

headline: Racing Mr. Jay to Jerusalem
summary: Roosevelt shoots a kestrel and a lark, then rides to Jerusalem, outracing Mr. Jay on horseback. He finds the city surprisingly small; the family stays at the Damascus Hotel.

events.detail: Kills a kestrel and a lark
Races Mr. Jay on horseback and wins

uncertain: 'Mr. Jay' assumed to be Augustus Jay of the Nile party.

headline: Holy Sepulchre and Gethsemane
summary: Roosevelt visits the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Garden of Gethsemane.

events.detail: Visits the Church of the Holy Sepulchre

headline: The Dome of the Rock
summary: Roosevelt sees the Mosque of Omar.

headline: Wailing Wall on Ellie's birthday
summary: After a morning hunt, Roosevelt goes to the Wailing Wall and the tombs of the judges and kings. Ellie turns thirteen.

events.detail: Sees the Tombs of the Judges and of the Kings

headline: Photographs and a ride
summary: Roosevelt visits a convent, buys photographs and goes riding.

headline: Sunday church in Jerusalem
summary: Roosevelt attends church in Jerusalem.

headline: Caravan to Jericho
summary: Roosevelt sets out on horseback for the Dead Sea over a rough road. The caravan counts some 35 pack animals and 25 people, with Bedouin guards, and camps near Jericho.

events.detail: Rides toward the Dead Sea with a large caravan and Bedouin guards

headline: Floating in the Dead Sea
summary: Roosevelt bathes in the Jordan, which strikes him as no bigger than a creek, then swims in the Dead Sea and finds he can't sink.

events.detail: Swims in the Dead Sea, unable to sink

headline: Bethlehem and the Nativity
summary: After a convent visit, the party rides to Bethlehem by way of the Pools of Solomon. Theodore Sr. pays guards to let them into the site of the Nativity.

events.detail: Theodore Sr. bribes their way into the Nativity site

uncertain: 'Pools of Jerusalem' likely the Pools of Solomon.

headline: Hebron and Abraham's Oak
summary: Roosevelt rides to Hebron, sees Abraham's Oak and the mosque, and goes shooting.

events.detail: Sees Abraham's Oak and the mosque

headline: Rain in Jerusalem
summary: Back in Jerusalem, the day is rainy.

headline: Riding back to Ramleh
summary: The party rides to Ramleh.

headline: Farewell to a horse named Grant
summary: Roosevelt rides to Jaffa and boards ship, where he is seasick. He is sad to say goodbye to the horse he rode and named Grant.

events.detail: Rides to Jaffa and boards ship

headline: Asthma in Beirut
summary: The family sails to Beirut and stays at the Hotel d'Orient. Roosevelt rides a horse and suffers an asthma attack.

headline: Trying out horses
summary: In Beirut the party tests horses for the overland trip.

headline: Seven hours to Ain Tufeh
summary: A ride of about seven hours brings the party to Ain Tufeh. Roosevelt and Ellie are stuck with poor mounts.

events.detail: Rides about seven hours to Ain Tufeh
He and Ellie have poor horses

headline: Off the Diligence Road to Abla
summary: The party follows the Diligence Road until lunch, then turns off and meets people at Abla.

events.detail: Follows the Diligence Road, then branches off

headline: The ruins of Baalbek
summary: A three-hour canter from Abla brings Roosevelt to the grand ruins of Baalbek, where he shoots a finch.

headline: A cold night in tents
summary: After shooting several birds in the morning, the party rides to Syrahayi and spends a bitterly cold night in tents.

events.detail: Camps in tents in the cold

uncertain: Place name as given; not identified.

headline: Asthma and stomach sickness
summary: The party rides to Sukr El Wady. That night Roosevelt is struck by a severe asthma attack along with cholera morbus.

events.detail: Bad asthma attack and cholera morbus

headline: Chasing jackals toward Damascus
summary: On a showery day Roosevelt hunts and spots jackals that had killed a goat; he gives chase but they escape. The party reaches Damascus.

headline: Haggling in the bazaar
summary: Roosevelt sees the horse market in Damascus and bargains in the bazaars for a suit.

events.detail: Bargains for a suit in the bazaars

headline: Up a minaret of 220 steps
summary: Roosevelt tours the Mosque of St. John, climbs a 220-step minaret for the view, and goes shooting with the British consul.

events.detail: Visits the Mosque of St. John

headline: Several birds near Damascus
summary: Roosevelt goes shooting and brings back several birds.

headline: Consulate men to dinner
summary: After another day of shooting, men from the British consulate dine with the family.

events.detail: British consulate staff come to dinner

headline: Ten changes of horses to Beirut
summary: On the road back to Beirut, Roosevelt sees gazelles; the party switches horses ten times.

events.detail: Rides to Beirut, changing horses ten times

headline: Ellie falls ill
summary: In Beirut, Ellie is sick; Roosevelt goes to church.

headline: Dinner at the Blisses'
summary: Roosevelt and Conie dine with Mr. Bliss and his family while Ellie remains ill.

events.detail: Dines at the Bliss home with Conie

headline: Boarding an Austrian steamer
summary: The family sails from Beirut at seven aboard an Austrian steamer; Ellie is still sick.

events.detail: Leaves Beirut on an Austrian steamer

headline: Off Cyprus
summary: The steamer passes Cyprus. Ellie is still unwell.

headline: Birds land on deck
summary: Far from land, birds alight on the ship, and Roosevelt pays to have them so he can skin them. Ellie is still ill.

events.detail: Pays for birds caught on deck to skin them

headline: Specimens from the sailors off Rhodes
summary: The sea is too rough to land at Rhodes, but sailors catch specimens for Roosevelt. In the afternoon the ship runs along the coast of Asia Minor, and Ellie improves.

headline: Changing ships at Smyrna
summary: The steamer reaches Smyrna, where the family transfers to another ship.

events.detail: Arrives at Smyrna and changes ships

headline: Candy and tag on a paddle steamer
summary: On a small paddle-wheeler bound for Athens, Roosevelt buys candy, gets seasick and plays tag.

headline: First look at the Acropolis
summary: Seasick still, Roosevelt reaches Piraeus and takes a carriage up to Athens, where he sees the Acropolis. The men and women of the party lodge at separate hotels.

events.detail: Lands at Piraeus and drives to Athens
Men and women stay at two different hotels

headline: Touring ancient Athens
summary: By carriage, Roosevelt tours the ruins of the Olympieion, a Greek theater, the Acropolis and the Parthenon, in the rain.

headline: Areopagus, then a ship for Constantinople
summary: Roosevelt goes back to the Acropolis and climbs the Areopagus, then drives to Piraeus to board an Italian steamer for Constantinople.

events.detail: Returns to the Acropolis and climbs the Areopagus
Boards an Italian steamer at Piraeus for Constantinople

headline: Walking around Smyrna
summary: The steamer reaches Smyrna in the afternoon, and Roosevelt walks through the town.

headline: A late departure
summary: The steamer does not get under way until six in the evening.

headline: Through the Dardanelles
summary: The ship passes through the Dardanelles and the Sea of Marmara while Roosevelt plays on deck.

events.detail: Passes the Dardanelles and Sea of Marmara

headline: Ashore at Constantinople
summary: At Constantinople the family rows ashore, walks to the Hotel d'Angleterre, and attends church.

headline: Candle fight with the Lawrence boys
summary: Roosevelt rides out with Frank and Tom Lawrence, who stay for dinner and games of muggins. He, Ellie and Tom end up in a candle fight, flinging hot wax at each other. He writes Edith Carow, mentioning that he has lost his gun.

events.detail: Rides with Frank and Tom Lawrence
The Lawrence boys dine and play muggins
Candle fight with Ellie and Tom

letters.topic: News from Constantinople, including the loss of his gun

uncertain: 'Frank' assumed to be a Lawrence brother. Letter topic beyond the lost gun is not given.

headline: The old city walls
summary: Roosevelt visits the ancient walls and towers of Constantinople.

events.detail: Sees the old walls and towers

headline: Thrown from his horse
summary: Sightseeing on horseback while the others ride in carriages, Roosevelt is thrown. He sees the Süleymaniye Mosque and Hagia Sophia and is sick that night.

events.detail: Thrown by his horse while sightseeing
Visits the Süleymaniye Mosque and Hagia Sophia

headline: A quiet day in Constantinople
summary: Nothing much happens.

headline: A glimpse of the Sultan
summary: The Lawrences and Roosevelts go together to the Sultan's palace, and Roosevelt sees the Sultan.

events.detail: Visits the Sultan's palace with the Lawrences and sees the Sultan

uncertain: Sultan not named in source; Abdülaziz reigned in 1873.

headline: The Lawrences depart
summary: The Lawrence family leaves for Brindisi.

headline: Sunday church in Constantinople
summary: Roosevelt attends church.

headline: Midnight sailing into the Black Sea
summary: The family boards a steamer at ten in the evening and sets out at midnight across the Black Sea toward Romania.

events.detail: Boards a steamer and departs at midnight for the Black Sea

headline: Varna and a Danube riverboat
summary: Seasick, Roosevelt reaches Varna at six in the evening and transfers to a riverboat on the Danube.

headline: Up the green Danube, gasping
summary: The riverboat steams up the Danube all day through green, rolling country, and Roosevelt suffers a severe asthma attack.

events.detail: Sails up the Danube all day

uncertain: Source wording around the asthma note is garbled.

headline: From boat to train
summary: Between Serbia and Austria the family changes boats and then boards a train.

events.detail: Changes boats and takes a train

headline: Arriving in Pest
summary: The family reaches Pest around one o'clock, stays at the King of England Hotel, visits a picture gallery and climbs the hill.

headline: Vienna, and Father's exposition duties
summary: The family checks into the Grand Hotel in Vienna. Theodore Sr., who sits on the exposition's board of directors, prepares for its opening.

events.detail: Theodore Sr. readies for the exposition opening

headline: Sunday church in Vienna
summary: Roosevelt goes to church.

headline: An idle day in Vienna
summary: Nothing in particular fills the day.

headline: Cousins arrive in Vienna
summary: Cousin West Roosevelt, Frank, Aunt Mary and the Misses Tiny and Gertrude Roosevelt pay a visit. Roosevelt buys a rabbit, dissects it, and plays.

events.detail: Visit from West, Frank, Aunt Mary, Tiny and Gertrude Roosevelt

uncertain: 'J. W. Roosevelt' read as cousin West Roosevelt; 'Frank' assumed to be Frankie Roosevelt.

headline: In Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna; nothing more is recorded.

headline: In Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna; nothing more is recorded.

headline: In Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna; nothing more is recorded.

headline: In Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna; nothing more is recorded.

headline: In Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna; nothing more is recorded.

headline: A week of pleasant sameness
summary: Roosevelt sums up the past week in Vienna in his diary as pleasantly uneventful, spent skinning birds or rabbits. West leaves for Bonn, and Ellie and Theodore Sr. go to Dresden.

events.detail: Ellie and Theodore Sr. go to Dresden

tr_quotes.text: Last week spent in pleasant monotony

headline: Suits of armor at the Ambras collection
summary: Roosevelt goes to see the Ambras collection and its armor.

events.detail: Views the Ambras collection's suits of armor

headline: Panic on the Vienna exchange
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna as a financial panic hits the city.
